एक: Eka — the son of Raya. Bha. IX. 15. 2.
एकचक्र: Ekacakra — a son of Danu. Bhā. VI. 6. 31; Br. III. 6. 7; M. 6. 19; Vā. 68. 7; Vi. I. 21. 5.
एकच्छत्र: Ekachatra — ‘one umbrella’ of Mahāpadma. Br. III. 74. 140.
एकछत्र: Ekachatra — ‘one umbrella’ of Mahāpadma. Br. III. 74. 140.
एकत: Ekata — a son of Brahmā; came to see Kṛṣṇa at Syaman-tapañcaka. Bhā. X. 84. 5.
एकदन्त: Ekadanta — an attribute of Vighneśa. Br. III. 42. 8, 39; IV. 44. 66.
एकपर्णा: Ekaparṇā — one of the three daughters of Menā and Himavān; wife of Asita (Sita — M. P.) and mother of Devala; performed penance under a banyan tree; lived on a single leaf once in every 2000 years. Vā. 72. 7; Br. III. 8. 32; 9. 3; 10. 8, 11; M. 13. 8-9; Vā. 70. 27; 71. 4; 72. 9, 11, 17.
एकपाटला: Ekapāṭalā — One of the three daughters of Himavān and Menā; wife of Jaigīṣavya. Their mindborn sons were Śan-kha and Likhita. Performed penance under the wood of cerasus puddam; lived on a pāṭala once in every 2000 years. Br. III. 9. 3; 10. 8 & 20, 21; Vā. 71. 4; 72. 7-10, 18-9.
एकपाद: Ekapāda (I) — a Bhairava god. Br. IV. 20. 82.
Ekapāda (II) — a name of Vighneśa. Br. IV. 44. 68.
एकपिङ्गल: Ekapiṅgala — a name of the king of the Yakṣas. Vā. 41. 8.
एकराट्: Ekarāṭ — one becomes such by reciting Saptārciṣa in a śrāddha, also by princely gifts on that occasion.1 Prācīna-barhis was one.2 Sārvabhauma, son of Suvarman as:3 Mahāpadma as.4 1) Vā. 74. 30. 2) Br. II. 37. 25; III. 16. 57; Vā. 63. 24. 3) Vā. 99. 186. 4) Br. III. 74. 140.
एकलव्य: Ekalavya — King of Niṣadas; was stationed by Jarāsan-dha at the southern gate of Mathurā, and again on the southern gate during the seige of Gomanta;1 brought up by hunters.2 1) Bhā. X. 50. 11[4]; 52. 11[8]; Br. III. 71. 190. 2) Vā. 96. 187.
एकल: Ekalas — thirteen in number; lords of minor kingdoms; (Wilson's Mekalā). Vi. IV. 24. 58.
एकलिङ्ग: Ekaliṅgas — kings (thirty-two) contemporaneous with the ten Śiśunāgas. Br. III. 74. 137.
एकवीरा: Ekavīrā — the goddess enshrined at Saḥya hill; a mother goddess. M. 13. 40: 179. 17.
एकशृङ्ग: Ekaśṛṅga — a hill south of the Mānasa. Vā. 36. 24.
एकशृङ्गा: Ekaśṛṅgā — the queen of Śukra, formerly Yogotpatti, the pitṛ kanyā. Br. III. 10. 86-87.
एकाक्ष: Ekākṣa — a Dānava with manuṣya-dharma. Br. III. 6. 15; Vā. 68. 15.
एकाक्षा: Ekākṣā — a R. of the Ketumāla country. Vā. 44. 20.
एकादशरथ: Ekādaśaratha — the son of Daśaratha, and father of Śakuni. Br. III. 70. 44; Vā. 95. 43.
एकादशीव्रत: Ekādaśīvrata — observed by Nanda. Bhā. X. 28. 1.
एकानङ्गा: Ekānaṅgā — came to see Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā return-ing from Indra's Court. Bhā. X. [67 (V) 50].
एकाम्रनिलय: Ekāmranilaya (of Śiva) — is Kāñcī; during his separa-tion from Pārvatī, Śiva sat under the āmra tree, and through Lalitā's grace, was formally married to Pārvatī, when he went to Kailāsa. Br. IV. 5. 7; 40. 37-45; 44. 94.
एकाम्भकम्: Ekāmbhakam — a tīrtha sacred to the goddess Kīrtimati  — sacred to Pitṛs. M. 13. 29; 22. 51.
एकार: Ekāra — the 11th Manu from the 11th face of the fourteen faced deva of Piśaṅga colour. Vā. 26. 43.
एकार्णव: Ekārṇava — a condition of deluge when Brahmā emerges out of the waters, enveloping the universe. The Lord becomes Avyakta; now is the avatār of Hamsa-Nārāyaṇa;1 full of darkness; of 1000 devavarṣas or years.2 1) Br. IV. 1. 173, 181, 234; M. 166. 17; 167. 1 & 48; Vā. 100. 179. 2) Vā. 23. 110; 24. 8; 26-7.
एकार्षेय: Ekārṣeyas — one of the eleven Vasiṣṭha branches. Vā. 70. 90.
एकाष्टक: Ekāṣṭaka — the final form attained in Brahmaloka by Virajā, the mindborn daughter of Ājyapa Manes. M. 15. 24.
एकोद्दिष्टम्: Ekoddiṣṭam — to be performed every year; for this only three piṇḍas are prescribed; details of ritual. M. 18. 1 & 25; Vi. III. 13. 23, 40.
एरक: Erakas — the grass growing on the seashore, supposed to be grown out of the particles of the musala given birth to by Sāmba and thrown into the sea by the order of the Yādava king. Bhā. XI. 1. 22.
एलक: Elaka — a tīrtham sacred to Pitṛs. M. 22. 53.
एलापत्र: Elāpa(u)tra (I) — a 1000 headed Nāga; living with the sun for a part of the year; in the month of Nabha. Bhā. XII. 11. 37; Br. II. 23. 9; M. 6. 40; 126. 10; Vi. II. 10. 9.
Elāpatra (II) — a Kādraveya Nāga. Br. III. 7. 34.
एलापर्ण: Elāparṇa — the Nāga with the sun in Nabha and Nabha-sya (Āvaṇi and Puraṭṭāśi). Vā. 52. 10.
एलापुत्र: Elāputra — heard the Viṣṇu Purāṇa from Kambala and narrated it to Vedaśiras who went to Pātāla. Vi. VI. 8. 47-8.
एलापुरम्: Elāpuram — a tīrtham sacred to Pitṛs. M. 22. 50.
एलामुख: Elāmukha — a reptile of Pātāla. M. 163. 56.
